extracted.intended_audience: ASSIST / eRA Commons users (PD/PI, Signing Officials, Administrative Officials, grant applicants and administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, validation rules, and UI workflows for preparing, previewing, managing, and submitting grant and non-research amendment applications using ASSIST (Application Submission System & Interface for Submission Tracking) integrated with eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Field Validations
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the component forms in ASSIST include fields requesting required information that must exist before the application can be submitted. Required fields are marked with a red asterisk (*). Although the information in these fields is required for submission, component forms can be saved without this information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When saving a form with missing required fields, a notice displays indicating that data entry errors were found and providing the options to Continue saving the form as-is or to Return to correct errors. Required fields must be provided before submission; saving without them is allowed for in-progress work so forms can be started and completed later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing Information Identification (summary icon and validation)
rubrics_metrics.description: To aid in the identification of incomplete forms, ASSIST employs a missing information icon - a red exclamation point (!) - on the summary page of incomplete component forms. The icon indicates the section or field with missing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the icon is seen on the summary page, edit the appropriate section and provide the required information before saving again. NOTE: Not all forms contain summary pages. Missing required information can also be identified by performing a component validation (see Validating an Individual Component).

rubrics_metrics.name: Add Optional Forms limited to FOA-allowed forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional forms may exist depending on the funding opportunity and may be added using the Add Optional Form feature. Only the optional forms available for the specific funding opportunity can be added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-project: Select Add Optional Form, choose from the drop-down list, Submit, then select the tab of the form to enter information. Multi-project: from Application Information expand component type, open Component Information, select Add Optional Form, choose and Submit, then select the tab to enter info. Cancel closes the window without adding the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change Component Order rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Change Component Order screen is used to set the order in which your components appear in the submitted application (i.e., the PDF version) for each particular component type. This is applicable only to multi-project applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can reorder components within a component type but cannot re-arrange the order of component types. Use the Order text box to enter a unique order value for each component. Duplicate order values produce an error. You may use decimal numbers (up to 2 places) and negative numbers to avoid re-numbering every component (e.g., 1.5). Use Refresh to display updated order (refresh does not save). Cancel aborts action; Save persists results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delete Component privileges and irreversible deletion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Delete Component feature allows permanently deleting individual components of any status from a multi-project application. This feature is available only to the Signing Official, Administrative Official, PI of the lead organization, and/or users with Entire Application Editor privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deleting components is permanent and irreversible; once deleted a component cannot be accessed, retrieved, or viewed. Deletion requires a two-step confirmation (Go Back or Continue at each prompt). You cannot delete a component if one or more of its forms are locked by yourself or another ASSIST user; a specific error will display listing the locked form(s). When a component is deleted the Application Information screen displays 'Component successfully deleted' and the Application Status History reflects the action with Status 'Abandoned' and a Status Comment indicating the deletion and user who performed it. Note: ASSIST also has a Delete Application feature for deleting an entire application (components need not be deleted first).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Submission Status definitions (multi-project)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a multi-project application evolves, its status is updated to reflect the current stage in the submission process. Statuses include: Work in Progress, All Components Final, All Components Validated, Ready for Submission, Submitted, Submission Errors, Abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: Work in Progress: allows editing; All Components Final: all components are Final (if not Abandoned) and ready for Validate Application; All Components Validated: system-generated when Validate Application runs error-free; Ready for Submission: manual status set after internal reviews; Submitted: system-generated after submitting to Grants.gov; Submission Errors: system-generated when validation returned errors; Abandoned: manual status indicating no longer being worked on. See flow figure for typical progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid application/component status changes and submission conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: There are defined valid status transitions and special conditions (multi- and single-project). For multi-project applications: Work in Progress >> All Components Final >> All Components Validated >> Ready for Submission >> Submitted is the normal flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special conditions: In order for an application to be submitted, at least one component of the application must be marked as Final. All other components must be in Final or Abandoned status. Some transitions are system-generated (e.g., All Components Validated set by ASSIST). The user must follow the valid status change rules listed in the Update Application Submission Status topic and the provided tables for multi- and single-project applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid Component Status Changes (allowed transitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST users with appropriate privilege may update an individual component's status. Valid component status changes are constrained (e.g., Work in Progress -> Complete / Final / Abandoned; Complete -> Abandoned; Final -> Work in Progress).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: An Overall component cannot be abandoned. See the Valid Component Status Changes table for exact allowed transitions and special conditions. At least one component must be Final to submit an application; components not in the proper statuses can block certain application status updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update Component Status process and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: To update a component status: from the Application Information page select the component and click Update Component Status. The Update Status window opens allowing selection of the new status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the update by optionally entering a comment and selecting Add comment or continue without adding a comment. A notification of the change in status is sent to appropriate individual(s) and the application status is changed to the selected status. When marking a component Final, ASSIST validates that no senior/key person bio-sketch exists on another component marked Final (only one bio-sketch per senior/key person may exist on an application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Component and Application Status History fields
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST maintains status history records for both components and applications. The Component Status History and Application Status History pages display key information for each status change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed fields include: Status Date (time/date of update), Status (the status value), Status Comment (comments regarding the status update; optional), Status Type (for applications: ASSIST, Grants.gov, or Agency), and Update User (who updated the status; may be ASSIST or Last Name, First Name). Use View Status History to inspect changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating and viewing preview of entire application
rubrics_metrics.description: Users with appropriate privileges may generate, view, print, and/or locally save a preview of the entire application image (PDF) from the Preview Application screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To generate an initial preview select Generate Preview; ASSIST queues the request. The preview request status may be Waiting to Process, Processing, Failed, or Preview Available. Use Refresh Status to update progress; when processing completes the View button appears. If another ASSIST user generated a preview concurrently you may see the error: 'A 'Generate Preview' request is pending for this application.' You may view, print, and save the PDF in a separate window when available. Viewing a previously generated image uses the View button in the request table. Generating a new preview replaces the prior image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previewing a component or form (component/form-level preview rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: With appropriate privileges users may preview an application's forms or individual components. You can preview the current form while working on it, or preview the current component (multi-project only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preview Current Form: select form tab, Preview Current Form, choose option to open PDF which displays in a new window; optionally print or save. Preview Current Component: from Component Information select Preview Current Component; a PDF is generated showing component forms and attachments. NOTE: Application and component summaries and tables of contents are generated only when previewing the entire application, not for individual components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Research Amendments initiation and ASSIST pre-population
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-research users initiate amendment applications via eRA Commons (role PD/PI or SO) using Manage Post Award Amendments; ASSIST is then opened and the application is pre-populated with the required forms and select data fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible users see only grants they are PD/PI on (checkbox to show expired grants is available). The Initiate button opens a menu of amendment types (Budget Revision, Carryover Request, Change in Scope, Key Personnel, Merger/Transfer/etc, No-Cost Extension, Organization Change). Clicking an option opens ASSIST with the forms required for that amendment type. The SF424 and Sites forms are always required for these amendment applications. Some fields in SF424 and other forms are pre-populated (some editable, some read-only) from eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-populated SF424 fields and read-only fields for Non-Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain SF424 fields are pre-populated when creating non-research amendment applications; some of those fields are editable while others are read-only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed pre-populated/read-only fields include: 1. Type of Submission (Pre-populated and Read-only); 2. Type of Application, letter (for Revision type), description in Other (if Revision type 'E: Other' is selected) (Pre-populated and Read-only); 3. Date Received (Automatically populated at submission time with the current date); 5. Federal Award Identifier (Pre-populated and Read-only); 8. a-d (Legal name, Tax ID number, DUNS, UEI, and address) (Pre-populated; DUNS and UEI are Read-only); 10. Name of Federal Agency (Pre-populated); 11. CFDA Number and Title (Pre-populated); 12. Funding Opportunity number and Title (Pre-populated and Read-only); 13. Competition ID Number and Title (Pre-populated); 15. Description of Project (Pre-populated); 16. Applicant and Program/Project (Pre-populated); 17. Start and End Date (Start Date is Pre-populated and Read-only and End Date is pre-populated); 18. Estimated Funding (pre-populated with '0.00'). NOTE: All fields with an asterisk [*] are required to be completed in order to submit the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Competing Continuation notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: SAMHSA grantees using ASSIST for non-competing continuation applications receive scheduled notifications about upcoming due dates and availability of the application package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PD/PI and Business Official (BO) are notified via email of the upcoming due date. The application package is available three (3) months before the due date or six (6) months before the current budget period end date. A reminder email is sent one (1) month before the due date. If the application has not been submitted by the due date, a late notice email is sent the next day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms required for Non-Research amendment packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on the funding opportunity and amendment type, a combination of standard and amendment-specific forms will be included in the ASSIST application package for non-research amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms listed (examples) include: SF424; SF424A (Budget Information – Non-Construction Programs); SF424B (Assurances for Non-Construction); SF424C (Budget Information for Construction Programs); SF424D (Assurances for Construction Programs); SFLLL (Disclosure of Lobbying Activities); Project Abstract Summary; Budget Narrative Attachment; Project Narrative Attachment; Other Attachments. Instructions URLs are provided for each form. Note that SF424 and Sites are always required for amendment applications.
